name: Raman Open Database (ROD): experimental mineral Raman spectra (frozen 2026-10-20 snapshot)
description: Experimental Raman spectra of minerals and related phases from the Raman Open Database (ROD, SOLSA project; El Mendili et al. 2019, doi:10.1107/S1600576719004229), served as a frozen snapshot of the continuously growing live database (bulk result.php?format=zip download of 2026-10-20: 1,133 CIF entry files; mirrored in the raman_data HuggingFace mirror repo and pinned by size and sha256, provenance in the snapshot MANIFEST.txt). 1,098 spectra of 432 labeled mineral/phase entries, resampled onto the common 250-1,200 cm^-1 @1 cm^-1 grid (951 points) that 98.5% of the snapshot's 1,115 experimental spectra fully cover. Excluded from the snapshot: 18 entries with only theoretical (DFT) spectra and the 17 experimental spectra not fully covering the common window. Labels use _chemical_name_mineral, falling back to _chemical_name_systematic, then _chemical_formula_sum (the .rod files carry values on the same line, on the next line, or in multi-line ';'-blocks, and the loader parses all three forms), so the 432 labels mix IMA mineral names with systematic names and formulas for unassigned phases and solid solutions. 108 labels have a single spectrum and 213 have two; most frequent: Andradite (22), Corundum (17), Anorthite (15). Excitation wavelengths: 532 nm (483), 780 nm (408), 633 nm (102), 785 nm (58), 514 nm (31), 488 nm (15), 632.8 nm (1); instruments dominated by Thermo Nicolet Almega XR (795) and DXR (154). Intensities are in arbitrary units (per-entry normalization is not documented); no preprocessing is applied here beyond grid resampling. group_ids = label: all spectra of one mineral/phase form one group (432 groups), so grouped k-fold CV is leave-one-mineral-species-out. Many entries overlap with the rruff_mineral_raw/preprocess datasets (~234 of the 1,115 experimental entries, ~21%, per the 2026-10-20 research -- the public-domain RRUFF spectra are mirrored in both databases); use the group ids to keep the two datasets on the same side of a fold. License: public domain -- all ROD data have been placed in the public domain by the contributors.

rai:dataCollection: Raman Open Database (ROD, SOLSA project): community-driven open-access database of Raman spectra (and XRD patterns) of minerals; contributors deposit spectra measured on various laboratory instruments with 488-785 nm excitation. This loader serves a frozen 2026-10-20 snapshot (1,133 CIF entry files), mirrored on the raman_data HuggingFace mirror and pinned by size and sha256.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: None applied by the loader beyond resampling onto the common 250-1,200 cm^-1 @1 cm^-1 grid (951 points) by linear interpolation. As-deposited intensities are in arbitrary units; per-entry device-specific baseline correction / normalization varies by source and is not documented per entry in the snapshot.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Mineral/phase labels taken from the .rod entry files' CIF metadata: _chemical_name_mineral (IMA mineral name) with fallback to _chemical_name_systematic, then _chemical_formula_sum; unassigned phases and solid solutions therefore carry systematic names or formulas. All 1,098 loaded spectra resolve a label (432 distinct labels); no human annotation involved.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive information is included; all spectra originate from mineral and phase samples without individual human identifiers.
rai:dataBiases: Spectra were acquired on a wide range of instruments (Thermo Nicolet Almega XR ~795, DXR 154, Aramis 53, T64000 31, others) and excitation wavelengths (532 nm 483, 780 nm 408, 633 nm 102, 785 nm 58, 514/488/632.8 nm 47), so intensities and baseline shapes are not comparable across entries; per-entry normalization is not documented. Class balance is strongly uneven: 108 labels have a single spectrum, 213 have two, the most frequent (Andradite) 22. ~21% of the entries (~234 of the 1,115 experimental) overlap with the public-domain RRUFF library mirrored in the rruff_mineral_* datasets, so entries shared between the two databases must be kept on the same side of a split (group ids).
rai:dataLimitations: Spectral library data with heterogeneous provenance: per-entry preprocessing (baseline, normalization) varies by source and is not documented per entry; intensities are in arbitrary units and include negative baseline points. Excluded from the snapshot: 18 entries with only theoretical (DFT) spectra and the 17 experimental spectra that do not fully cover the common 250-1,200 cm^-1 window (no extrapolation). Many mineral entries overlap with the RRUFF database (mirrored in the rruff_mineral_* datasets).
rai:dataSocialImpact: Supports automated mineral identification and phase analysis for geology, materials science, and art conservation, and provides a public-domain benchmark for Raman classification models.
rai:dataUseCases: Multi-class mineral/phase identification (432 classes), spectral library matching, and benchmarking of classification models on heterogeneous multi-instrument Raman data. Grouped k-fold CV is leave-one-mineral-species-out (group = label, 432 groups).
prov:wasGeneratedBy: Data collection: experimental Raman spectra of minerals and related phases from a frozen 2026-10-20 snapshot of the Raman Open Database (ROD, SOLSA; El Mendili et al. 2019, doi:10.1107/S1600576719004229). 1,133 CIF entry files from the bulk zip download; 1,098 experimental spectra loaded (18 theoretical-only entries and 17 partial-window spectra excluded); resampled onto the common 250-1,200 cm^-1 @1 cm^-1 grid. Preprocessing: none applied by the loader; per-entry device-specific preprocessing varies by source and is not documented. Annotation: labels from the _chemical_name_mineral, _chemical_name_systematic, or _chemical_formula_sum CIF fields (fallback chain), covering same-line, next-line, and multi-line ';'-block values.
